content.title: How to watch Warriors vs Rockets without cable tonight
content.text: Steph Curry returns as the Warriors host the Rockets at Chase Center with playoff positioning on the lineBilly CaddenSunday night brings one of the most anticipated matchups of the late NBA season as the Warriors host the Rockets at Chase Center, with a major storyline headlining the game. After missing 27 straight games with a lingering right knee injury, Steph Curry is set to return to the floor, giving Golden State a much-needed boost heading into the Play-In tournament. Without Curry, the Warriors have managed to stay afloat at 36-41 and lock in the No. 10 seed, but with Jimmy Butler and Moses Moody out for the season, they’ll need Curry to shake off the rust quickly if they want to make any noise.The Rockets come into this one at 48-29, sitting in 5th place in the Western Conference and right in the middle of a tight seeding battle. After a turbulent stretch, Houston has found its rhythm again, winning five straight and stabilizing themselves with just a handful of games left. With only a couple of games separating seeds three through six, every outcome matters, especially with a potential first-round matchup against Denver looming. And beyond the playoff implications, this game offers something special — another chapter in the Steph Curry vs. Kevin Durant rivalry, one of the defining matchups of this era after winning two championships together, and it’s one that fans won’t get many more chances to see.The Warriors vs Rockets game tips off Sunday night at 7:00 p.m. PST/9:00 p.m. CST, and fans across the country can watch it with Sling TV and Peacock.When is Warriors vs Rockets? What: Golden State Warriors vs Houston Rockets When: Sunday, April 5, 2026, at 7:00 p.m. PST/9:00 p.m. CST Where: Chase Center, San Francisco, CA TV: NBC and Peacock How to stream the Warriors vs Rockets game without cableWith Steph Curry returning to play and the game being a showdown against his old teammate Kevin Durant, the Warriors vs. Rockets game will air nationally on NBC and Peacock. While you could just sign up for Peacock to watch this game, that’ll only get you access to NBA games that air on NBC. To catch as many games as possible, especially with the NBA playoffs right around the corner, we suggest signing up for a streaming platform that offers live sports, like Sling TV.Depending on your zip code, Sling Select may carry NBC in your area and start at just $19.99/month. If Select isn’t available to you, Sling Blue starts at $45.99/month, depending on where you live, and also carries NBC. Here are all the ways you can tune into Sunday’s game with Sling: Sling TV 3-Month Prepay (Starting at $49.99 - $159.99 then monthly recurring payments) Sling TV Select (Starting at $19.99/month) Sling TV Blue (Starting at $45.99/month) Sling TV Orange & Blue (Starting at $60.99/month) Unfortunately, NBC is not available on Sling everywhere, so make sure it is before signing up. If not, you can sign up for any of the other top streaming platforms below to catch the game: fuboTV ($48.99 for the first month, then $73.99/month with a 7-day free trial) DIRECTV STREAM ($89.99/month; there are no free trials right now for the base plan) Hulu + Live TV ($89.99/month with a 3-day free trial; also includes Disney+ and ESPN+) YouTube TV ($67.99/month for the first three months, then $82.99/month with a variable free trial) April 5, 2026Andrew Koopman is a freelance writer who's been producing content since 2020. If he's not writing, Andrew is almost certainly watching sports (go Warriors!) or planning his next adventure as he attempts to visit all 50 states in the next few years.
